mascot.name: Bernie Brewer
mascot.hometown: Milwaukee County Stadium scoreboard, Milwaukee, WI
mascot.headshot_credit: Wikimedia Commons, 'Bernie Brewer in crowd' (CC license; see file page)

stats_2026.Debut: 1973 (chalet opened at the April 14, 1973 home opener)
stats_2026.Origin: Milt Mason, 69, lived ~40 days atop the County Stadium scoreboard in 1970 until the Brewers drew 40,000
stats_2026.Slide: Down a slide from Bernie's Dugout above the left-field bleachers after every Brewers home run

mascot.postseason_2026: Has slid after every Brewers postseason home run at American Family Field; 7 Brewers homers in the NLCS alone
mascot.card_back: In June 1970 a 69-year-old fan named Milt Mason climbed into a trailer on top of the County Stadium scoreboard and vowed to stay until the brand-new Brewers drew a crowd of 40,000. It took about 40 days, and on Bat Day, August 16, 1970, 44,387 showed up and he slid down a rope, burning his hands and legs. The team turned him into a mustachioed, lederhosen-wearing character in 1973 with a beer-barrel chalet, from which Bernie slid into a giant beer mug after every homer. The chalet was torn out in 1984, fans voted him back in 1993, and today he slides from Bernie's Dugout above left field. The original chalet now lives at Lakefront Brewery, on the brewery tour.
mascot.weird_fact: The original 1973 beer-barrel chalet survives on display at Lakefront Brewery in Milwaukee, and Bernie's slide platform was briefly renamed the Kalahari Splash Zone after a 2009 sponsorship deal. He joined Twitter in April 2010 and has the largest following of any MLB mascot there.

mascot_extra.name: Famous Racing Sausages
mascot_extra.headshot_credit: Wikimedia Commons, 'Sausage Racers' (CC license; see file page)

stats_2026.When: Middle of the 6th inning, every Brewers home game
stats_2026.Roster: #1 Brat, #2 Polish, #3 Italian, #4 Hot Dog, #5 Chorizo (sombrero)
stats_2026.2026 wins (through Sept. 13): Polish 21, Italian 19, Chorizo 14, Hot Dog 12, Brat 11

mascot_extra.postseason_2026: Games 1 and 2 are the first World Series games the sausages have ever raced in; the Brewers' only previous World Series (1982) predates the race.
mascot_extra.card_back: Five seven-foot foam sausages sprint from third base around home toward first in the middle of the sixth inning at every Brewers home game. It started as a cartoon race on the County Stadium scoreboard in the early 1990s, and the first live race was June 27, 1993. The Hot Dog joined mid-decade, and Chorizo ran once in 2006 for Cerveceros Day before MLB's no-new-mascots-midseason rule made him wait until 2007 to join full time. On Sundays the big sausages hand off to the Little Weenies. Watch the Polish Sausage: the team bio says he starts slow and finishes strong, and he leads the 2026 standings.
mascot_extra.weird_fact: On July 9, 2003, Pirates first baseman Randall Simon whacked the Italian Sausage with a bat mid-race, knocking over the runner (Mandy Block) and the Hot Dog. He was arrested, fined and suspended three games, and Block asked only for the autographed bat. In 2013 the Italian Sausage costume was stolen from a curling club and turned up at a Cedarburg bar 12 days later.

stats_2026.Height: Tall enough to ride the rides at Disney World (seadogs run 5 to 6 feet)
stats_2026.Favorite food: Popcorn, cotton candy and hot dogs
stats_2026.Dislikes: Baths, fur in his food, nacho cheese in his fur

mascot.postseason_2026: First World Series since 2020; Game 3 on Oct. 26 will be the first World Series game at Tropicana Field since 2008
mascot.card_back: Raymond is a shaggy blue creature with a baseball for a nose, oversized sneakers and a backward cap. The Rays' official story is that scouts on a Gulf of Mexico fishing trip lured him to the boat with the smell of hot dogs, and that he belongs to a previously undiscovered dog species, the 'seadog.' He debuted June 21, 1998 in the Devil Rays' first season and has outlasted the Devil, the name change, and two stadium sagas. He lists his position as 'all of them' and his hobbies as full-contact shuffleboard and extreme checkers.
mascot.weird_fact: The Rays claim a team of marine biologists and zoologists formally identified his species in 2005 as 'Canus Manta Whatthefluffalus.' His colleague DJ Kitty was reportedly found near the dumpsters behind Tropicana Field.
mascot.texas_tie: The Rays' last World Series (2020, vs. the Dodgers) was played entirely at Globe Life Field in Arlington, TX, so Raymond's only prior Fall Classic was in Texas. He is also officially 'born in the Gulf of Mexico,' which laps the Texas coast.

MIL.name: Jacob Misiorowski
MIL.postseason_2026: 2 starts, 8.1 IP, 3 ER, 11 K; won NLDS G1 and NLCS G1 but has not finished the 5th inning in either
MIL.card_back: 'The Miz' is a 6-foot-7 right-hander from Grain Valley, Missouri, who went to a junior college (Crowder) instead of LSU and became the hardest-throwing starter in baseball history. In 2026 he led MLB in ERA (1.80), WHIP (0.80) and strikeouts (252), hit 105.5 mph on June 26, and is the presumptive NL Cy Young winner. He threw 57 pitches at 100-plus in one game in May, an MLB record, and he collects Pokemon cards.
MIL.weird_fact: On June 26, 2026 he threw a 105.5 mph fastball, the fastest pitch ever recorded by a starting pitcher, and on September 8 he became the first pitcher ever to throw 1,000 pitches at 100-plus mph in one season.

TB.name: Nick Martinez
TB.postseason_2026: 2 starts, 9.0 IP, 3 ER, 6 K; held Cleveland to 1 run over 5.1 IP in ALCS G4; first postseason starts of his career
TB.card_back: A Miami kid who was a second baseman at Fordham until the Rangers drafted him as an 18th-round pitcher in 2011. After four years in Texas and four in Japan (a 1.60 ERA for SoftBank in 2021 and an Olympic silver medal), he came back to the Padres and Reds, and at 36 made his first All-Star team on a one-year, $13 million Rays deal: 15-6, 3.10 ERA, 180 innings, and the lowest walk rate in baseball. Kevin Cash picked him over ace Drew Rasmussen for Game 1. He hosts a team dinner in every road city, and took the Rays to a Milwaukee steakhouse Wednesday night.
TB.weird_fact: He was mostly a second baseman in college (.295, 22 steals at Fordham) with only 15 relief appearances before being drafted as a pitcher. Now he organizes a team dinner in every road city, including a Milwaukee steakhouse this week.
TB.texas_tie: Drafted by the Texas Rangers (18th round, 2011). Pitched for Texas 2014-2017 with minor-league stops at Frisco and Round Rock.

games.pitching_note: Rays manager Kevin Cash announced Thursday that Nick Martinez, not ace Drew Rasmussen, starts Game 1, to give Rasmussen an extra day after a heavy postseason workload. Misiorowski starts on 11 days' rest.

MIL.name: Jackson Chourio
MIL.postseason_2026: .171 AVG but 2 HR and 7 RBI in 8 games, including a game-tying homer in NLDS G1 and a walk-off single in NLDS G2
MIL.card_back: Signed out of Maracaibo, Venezuela, for $1.9 million at 16, Chourio got an eight-year, $82 million contract in December 2023 before he had played a big-league game, then debuted on Opening Day 2024 as the youngest player in the majors. He is the only player ever with three 20-homer, 20-steal seasons before turning 23, and he already owns the Brewers' career postseason RBI record. He won WBC gold with Venezuela in March 2026 with a hand he broke during the tournament.
MIL.weird_fact: His $82 million extension (Dec. 4, 2023) was the largest contract ever given to a player who had never appeared in an MLB game.

MIL.name: Jake Bauers
MIL.postseason_2026: 2026 NLCS MVP: go-ahead HR in Game 3 at Dodger Stadium, 6 RBI in the series
MIL.card_back: A seventh-round pick who had been a Ray, an Indian, a Mariner and a Yankee, Bauers hit .199 for Milwaukee in 2024, was cut loose, and came back on a minor-league deal. In 2026 he led the Brewers with 26 home runs, posted a .389 on-base percentage, and won NLCS MVP. He had planned to retire after 2024 and came back in part for the health insurance when his wife was pregnant.
MIL.weird_fact: He was set to retire after the 2024 season and returned to baseball partly for health insurance after his wife became pregnant. Two years later he was NLCS MVP.

MIL.name: Christian Yelich
MIL.postseason_2026: .292 in 7 games with 2 steals; still chasing his first World Series ring
MIL.card_back: The 2018 NL MVP and two-time batting champion came to Milwaukee from Miami in January 2018 and became the face of the franchise. On September 26, 2026 the Brewers named him the first captain in team history, and his great-grandfather Fred Gehrke played in the NFL. He is the only player ever to hit for the cycle three times against the same team (the Reds: twice in 2018, once in 2022).
MIL.weird_fact: He is the only player in MLB history with three cycles against the same opponent, all against the Cincinnati Reds, and he appeared as himself on Magnum P.I. in 2019.

MIL.name: William Contreras
MIL.postseason_2026: The best hitter in the 2026 playoffs: .367/.457/.700, 3 HR, 11 hits in 8 games, including a go-ahead HR in NLDS G1
MIL.card_back: The younger brother of Willson Contreras, William won a World Series ring with the 2021 Braves, made the 2022 All-Star team, and came to Milwaukee in the December 2022 three-team Sean Murphy trade. He has two Silver Sluggers (2023, 2024), finished fifth in the 2024 NL MVP vote, and the local writers call him the team's heartbeat. MIL.name: Brice Turang
MIL.postseason_2026: 6-for-11 with 5 walks in the NLCS; 6 runs scored in 8 postseason games

His first MLB homer was a grand slam in the 2023 home opener, in 2024 he led the majors with 50 stolen bases and won both the Gold Glove and the Platinum Glove at second base, and he drove in 100 runs in 2026. His sister Brianna is married to NFL punter Tress Way.
MIL.weird_fact: In 2024 he won the Gold Glove and Platinum Glove at second base, led MLB with 50 steals, and had the lowest pull percentage of any hitter in the majors (26.4%).

MIL.name: Garrett Mitchell
MIL.postseason_2026: 2 HR in the NLCS, both decisive; 6 runs scored in 8 postseason games
MIL.card_back: A UCLA center fielder who set the Bruins' single-season triples record, Mitchell was Milwaukee's first-round pick in 2020. He has played with Type 1 diabetes since age 9 on an insulin pump, and through a brutal run of injuries (shoulder, broken hand, oblique), then stayed healthy in 2026 for 145 games and two big NLCS home runs. MIL.name: Sal Frelick
MIL.postseason_2026: 3-for-15 with 4 walks and 2 steals in 5 games; sat against some lefties
MIL.card_back: A Lexington, Massachusetts quarterback who threw 30 touchdown passes as a high school senior, Frelick turned down a Boston College football scholarship to play baseball there instead. MIL.name: David Hamilton
MIL.postseason_2026: 5-for-11 (.455) with a HR and 3 steals in 4 games; has started at 3B against right-handers
MIL.card_back: A San Marcos native out of San Marcos High and the University of Texas, Hamilton tore his Achilles in an electric scooter accident in 2019, signed with Milwaukee anyway as an eighth-rounder, went to Boston in the Hunter Renfroe trade, and came back to the Brewers in February 2026. MIL.weird_fact: He tore his Achilles tendon in an electric scooter accident in 2019, costing him his junior year at Texas, and he once stole six bases in one game, a Wisconsin Timber Rattlers record.
MIL.texas_tie: Born and raised in San Marcos, TX. San Marcos High School and the University of Texas at Austin, parents who played at Southwest Texas State, and Team Texas in 2020.

TB.name: Yandy Díaz
TB.postseason_2026: .308 with 2 HR, 4 doubles and a .905 OPS in 9 games; the only Ray with multiple postseason homers
TB.card_back: The 2023 AL batting champion (.330) defected from Cuba in 2013 on his third attempt, after two arrests. TB.texas_tie: His father Jorge, also a Cuban defector, briefly played in the Texas Rangers organization.

TB.weird_fact: Broke his left wrist in a collision with Giancarlo Stanton at first base on July 31, 2025, and missed two months of his All-Star season.

TB.name: Chandler Simpson
TB.postseason_2026: 6-for-25 with 3 steals and just 1 strikeout in 8 games

Simpson led Division I with a .434 average at Georgia Tech, stole 104 bases in the minors in 2024 (the most since 2012), and has led the AL in steals in both of his big-league seasons (44, then 46), hitting .306 with 175 hits in 2026. He has never hit a major-league home run, and he almost never strikes out.
TB.weird_fact: He has zero home runs in two full MLB seasons (0 in 2026) while leading the AL in stolen bases both years, and he is the fifth player ever with 40-plus steals in each of his first two seasons.

TB.name: Junior Caminero
TB.postseason_2026: .273/.351/.455 in 9 games; first career postseason HR in the ALCS Game 6 clincher
TB.card_back: Signed by Cleveland at 16 and stolen by the Rays in a 2021 trade for pitcher Tobias Myers, Caminero hit 45 homers in 2025 (one shy of the Rays record), reached the Home Run Derby final, and followed with 42 homers and 101 RBI in 2026 at age 23. He won WBC bronze with the Dominican Republic in March. His little brother is named Girardi, after Joe Girardi, at Junior's suggestion.
TB.weird_fact: His younger brother is named Girardi after former Yankees manager Joe Girardi, a name Junior suggested. In 2025 he led MLB in grounding into double plays (31) while hitting 45 home runs.
